headline: Bangladesh's gas crisis persists despite LNG supply recovery, impacting power generation
summary: Despite both floating LNG terminals resuming operations, gas supply remains at only 70% of capacity, leading to a significant shortfall against daily demand. This ongoing shortage is severely affecting electricity generation and industrial production across th
details: Bangladesh's LNG supply has recovered with both floating terminals at Maheshkhali back in operation, but the gas crisis is unlikely to ease significantly. Combined LNG send-out is expected to remain at around 70 percent of the two terminals’ combined capacity this week.

Gas supply is projected to stay around 2,380-2,430 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) against an estimated daily demand of about 3,800 mmcfd. This lingering shortage is set to put pressure on electricity generation, with gas-fired power plants unable to operate at full capacity.

Against a peak demand of around 17,500 megawatts (MW) this week, only about 15,500-16,000MW of generation is expected to be available. Although the country has approximately 29,500MW of installed generation capacity, much of it is unavailable due to various reasons, including fuel constraints.

According to a recent forecast by Power Grid Bangladesh, 82 of the country’s 143 power plants were either shut or generating below capacity. This was primarily due to fuel shortages or ongoing maintenance issues.

Fuel and maintenance problems at major coal-fired plants are also contributing to the generation shortfall. The three 1,320MW coal-based plants – Payra, Rampal, and RNPL Patuakhali – were each operating at roughly half their capacity.

RNPL Patuakhali’s generation was constrained by coal-related problems, while Payra has been facing a machine-related issue since July 28. At Rampal, one unit’s output was reduced around midnight on August 10.

Summit’s LNG terminal resumed supply on Friday evening after running out of LNG, now supplying around 500 mmcfd. The Excelerate Energy-operated FSRU also resumed operations but at half capacity, supplying up to 300 mmcfd.

Repair work on Excelerate's boiler, damaged in a July 21 fire, is expected to continue until Wednesday, with the timing for full capacity restoration uncertain. This means overall LNG send-out is expected to remain around 750-800 mmcfd in the coming days, against a combined capacity of 1,100 mmcfd.

This situation, while an improvement from recent complete shutdowns, does not restore the gas system to its already constrained normal position. Before the latest disruptions, the country typically supplied around 2,650 mmcfd against the 3,800 mmcfd demand.

The persistent gas shortage has already disrupted gas-fired power generation and industrial production. Factories have been operating at reduced capacity due to low gas pressure, and CNG stations have faced supply constraints and long queues.

headline_marked: [[Measles deaths cross 900]] in Bangladesh amid vaccination coverage concerns
headline: Measles deaths cross 900 in Bangladesh amid vaccination coverage concerns
summary: Measles continues to claim lives in Bangladesh, with the death toll now exceeding 900, nearly three months after a nationwide vaccination campaign concluded. Health experts cite vaccination gaps, comorbidities, and malnutrition as key factors in the ongoing ou
details: Measles continues to claim lives in Bangladesh, with the death toll crossing the 900-mark yesterday, indicating the outbreak is far from over. In the 24 hours to 8:00am yesterday, eight more children died with measles-like symptoms, taking the combined death toll to 902, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

Of the total, 803 deaths are suspected measles deaths and 99 are confirmed measles deaths. The latest figures also show that the pace of deaths has not slowed significantly, with the last 100 deaths recorded in just 23 days, compared with 26 days for the previous 100, according to an analysis of DGHS data.

Health experts and doctors said lack of vaccination, along with comorbidities, malnutrition, and delays in seeking hospital care, are major reasons behind the deaths. They attributed the continued outbreak to a gap in vaccination coverage affecting around 40 lakh children, infections among children outside the campaign’s target age group, and inadequate infection prevention and control measures.

At least 798 suspected and confirmed measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours to 8:00am yesterday, taking the total number of cases to 1.59 lakh. During the period, 700 patients were hospitalised with measles or measles-like symptoms, bringing the total number of hospital admissions to 1.23 lakh, according to the data.

The continued hospital admissions and deaths are raising fresh questions about the effectiveness of the emergency measles-rubella vaccination campaign. Doctors found that most admitted patients and those who died were unvaccinated.

Doctors at the three major facilities treating measles patients — DNCC Dedicated Covid-19 Hospital, Infectious Diseases Hospital (IDH), and Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute — reported that the number of patients has been rising lately. The number of patients declined after the vaccination drive in May but has been rising again in recent weeks.

Asif Haider, administrative officer of the DNCC hospital, stated that nearly 90 percent of the admitted patients are unvaccinated, while almost all those who died had not been vaccinated. He added that many children developed other viral infections after recovering from measles, which led to pneumonia and, ultimately, death.

Mirza Md Ziaul Islam, director of Bangladesh Shishu Hospital, noted that most of the deaths had comorbidities like heart and kidney problems. When children with such problems caught measles, their condition became critical, especially since most were also malnourished and unvaccinated.

DGHS Director General Pravath Chandra Biswas confirmed that they have taken a mop-up drive to expand measles coverage, which will be strengthened further to bring in unvaccinated children. They have also directed all hospitals to strictly maintain quarantine protocols to prevent the spread of the infection.
